DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO AUG 06 2025 ATTY. ALELI U. CONCEPCION Mayor Municipality of Balaoan La Union Dear Mayor Concepcion: This refers to your letter dated April 23, 2025, requesting this Department's legal opinion on whether electric cooperatives registered solely with the National Electrification Administration (NEA) may claim exemption from the payment of local taxes, fees, and charges pursuant to Section 32-A of Republic Act No. 10531, in relation to Sections 133 and 234 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). Per your representation, the La Union Electric Cooperative (LUELCO) asserts its entitlement to local tax exemptions, citing preferential rights granted to NEA-registered cooperatives under R.A. No. 10531, provided they meet NEA's financial and operational standards. While R.A. No. 10531 recognizes NEA's supervisory authority over electric cooperatives and grants certain incentives, it does not expressly confer tax exemption privileges, nor does it amend or repeal the tax provisions under the LGC. Thus, any claim for exemption must be grounded on clear statutory authority. It bears emphasizing that the 1987 Constitution, under Article X, Section 5, grants Local Government Units (LGUs) the power to create their own sources of revenue and to levy taxes, fees, and charges. This mandate is operationalized by the LGC, which expressly authorizes LGUs to impose taxes unless specifically exempted by law. In PHILRECA v. Department of the Interior and Local Government (G.R. No. 143076, June IO, 2003), the Supreme Court categorically ruled that the tax exemptions previously granted to electric cooperatives under Presidential Decree No. 269 were deemed withdrawn by the LGC. The Court held that tax exemptions must be expressly stated and are strictly construed against the taxpayer. The withdrawal of such exemptions was part of the legislative intent to strengthen local autonomy and the financial independence of LGUs. Furthermore, in City of Iriga v. CASURECO Ill (G.R. No. 192945, June 29, 2016), the Court clarified that only electric cooperatives duly registered with the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) may invoke the tax exemptions under the Cooperative Code and the LGC. NEA registration, standing alone, does not suffice. Accordingly, in the absence of registration with the CDA, electric cooperatives such as LUELCO may not legally claim exemption from the imposition of local taxes by "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

LGUs. Their continued entitlement to tax incentives hinges on compliance with the statutory requirement of CDA registration. This view is consistent with the constitutional policy of empowering LGUs and promoting fiscal autonomy through the exercise of their taxing powers, enabling them to fund essential services and reduce reliance on the national government. This opinion is rendered based solely on the facts and representations stated and without prejudice to any contrary interpretation by competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have provided sufficient guidance on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/RPB/LLLS-LLRALD/mag/kbm Page 2 of 2
